entities.summary:
Hua Xiong, also recorded in the annotated version of Zizhi Tongjian as Ye Xiong (葉雄), was a military general serving under the warlord Dong Zhuo during the late Eastern Han dynasty of China.

Hua Xiong's military campaigns played a crucial role in the brutal struggle for power among the warlords that followed the collapse of the Han dynasty in 189 CE. As Dong Zhuo's right-hand man, Hua Xiong was instrumental in the Battle of Pingyuan, a pivotal conflict that shaped the fate of China's warlords.

The legacy of Hua Xiong extends beyond his military achievements, as he represents a critical moment in China's tumultuous early imperial period. His involvement in the power struggles of the late Han dynasty laid the groundwork for the tumultuous Three Kingdoms period that followed.

Hua Xiong's story serves as a testament to the complex web of alliances and rivalries that defined ancient Chinese politics, as well as the devastating consequences of war on ordinary people.
